chunks: A man said to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, “Where should strangers relieve themselves?” So he said:
“They should avoid the banks of rivers, through roads, beneath fruit-bearing trees, and places of cursing.”
Then it was said to him, “And where are the places of cursing?” He said, “The doors of houses.”
“Allah has cursed the one who defecates in the shade of stopping places, the one who prevents access to frequented water, and the one who blocks the traveled road.”

key_terms.الطَّرِيقَ الْمَسْلُوكَ: a road that is commonly traveled
key_terms.الطُّرُقَ النَّافِذَةَ: public pass-through roads used by people
key_terms.شُطُوطَ الْأَنْهَارِ: the banks or edges of rivers
key_terms.ظِلِّ النُّزَّلِ: the shade of places where travelers stop or rest
key_terms.مَوَاضِعَ اللَّعْنِ: places that provoke people’s cursing because of harm or offense
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: used here in the sense of relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: Where is it forbidden or disliked to relieve oneself according to Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: These reports teach the etiquette and legal-ethical limits of relieving oneself in public or shared spaces. They prohibit causing harm, impurity, or offense near rivers, roads, fruit-bearing trees, resting places, water sources, and the entrances of homes, emphasizing respect for public welfare and the rights of others.
